## Findings
- claim-1: For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), the paper conjectures that both Theorem 5.4 generating sets of \(J_v\) are minimal; each has \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements, where \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6@L14-L27|claim=ordinary-document] [source-6@L35-L42|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: The stronger proposed reduction is \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\); the authors report that a proof had eluded them. [source-6@L56-L72|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-3: \(\Lambda\) has Schur \(\mathbb Z\)-basis, \(I_{r,n-r}\) is the ideal spanned by \(s_\lambda\) with \(\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\), and \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) has basis \(s_\lambda\) for \(\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\). [source-2@L1312-L1330|claim=formal-document]
- claim-4: The supplied paper states that \(J_v\) is generated in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by each of the two explicitly bounded Schur lists \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\) and \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\). [source-2@L1390-L1400|claim=formal-document]
- claim-5: The reported finite verification range is all bigrassmannian permutations with \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\); this is finite evidence, not a universal proof. [source-6@L46-L54|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-6: The only nonlocal search candidate with an abstract, “Model Reduction for Switched Differential-Algebraic Equations with Known Switching Signal,” concerns switched differential-algebraic equations and model reduction, not symmetric functions, Schubert ideals, indecomposables, or \(\operatorname{Tor}_0^\Lambda\); it supplies no applicable theorem. [doi:10.52825/dae-p.v3i.688]
- claim-7: If an abelian group \(Q\) is spanned by \(N\) elements and \(\dim_{\mathbb Q}(Q\otimes\mathbb Q)=N\), then \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\): the surjection \(\mathbb Z^N\to Q\) has kernel \(K\); tensoring gives \(\mathbb Q^N\to Q\otimes\mathbb Q\) an isomorphism, so \(K\otimes\mathbb Q=0\); since \(K\subseteq\mathbb Z^N\) is torsion-free, \(K=0\).
- claim-8: Establishing \(\dim_{\mathbb Q}(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\otimes\mathbb Q)=\binom{a+b}{a}\) would prove the stronger proposed freeness statement and hence minimality of either displayed \(N\)-element generating set.
- claim-9: No retrieved exact external theorem statement computes \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\), \(\operatorname{Tor}_0^\Lambda(\mathbb Z,J_v)\), or the relevant graded Betti numbers.
## Strategy
1. Retrieve exact formal passages for \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), admissible parameters, \(i,j\), grading, and homogeneity of \(J_v\). Until then, use the displayed generators only conditionally.

2. Run a bounded literature search with a preserved query log. Search exact phrases including:
   - `"bigrassmannian" "J_v" "minimal generators"`
   - `"v_{r,s,t,n}" Schur ideal`
   - `"J_v / Lambda_+ J_v"`
   - `"Schubert ideal" indecomposables`
   
   For every candidate, record theorem statement, hypotheses, and applicability to the integral quotient \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). The sole recorded nonlocal candidate is irrelevant by claim-6; this does not establish absence of applicable literature.

3. Conditional on graded homogeneity, set
   \[
   R=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r},\qquad R_d=\bigoplus_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\\|\lambda|=d}}\mathbb Zs_\lambda.
   \]
   Fix an ordering \(C_d\) of partitions in the rectangle of size \(d\). For \(\alpha\in C_k\), define the projected Littlewood--Richardson multiplication matrix
   \[
   T_{\alpha,e}:R_e\to R_{e+k},\qquad
   (T_{\alpha,e})_{\nu,\beta}=c_{\alpha,\beta}^{\nu}
   \quad(\nu\in C_{e+k},\ \beta\in C_e).
   \]

4. For either displayed generator list \(G\) from claim-4, construct degreewise lattices
   \[
   M_d=\sum_{\substack{\mu\in G,\ |\mu|\le d\\ \alpha\in C_{d-|\mu|}}}
   \mathbb Z\,T_{\alpha,|\mu|}e_\mu\subseteq R_d.
   \]
   If \(B_e\) is a column matrix generating \(M_e\), construct
   \[
   D_d=(\Lambda_+M)_d
      =\sum_{1\le k\le d}\ \sum_{\alpha\in C_k}
        \operatorname{colspan}_{\mathbb Z}(T_{\alpha,d-k}B_{d-k}).
   \]
   Then
   \[
   \dim_{\mathbb Q}(M_d/D_d\otimes\mathbb Q)
   =\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M_d-\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}D_d.
   \]
   Smith normal forms should additionally record possible integral torsion.

5. After source recovery fixes parameter filters, produce finite-range artifacts for the range reported in claim-5: enumerated parameters, generator lists, all matrices, rational ranks, Smith data, and
   \[
   \sum_d\dim_{\mathbb Q}(M_d/D_d\otimes\mathbb Q).
   \]
   This is implementation evidence only.

6. Continue to a universal target: index the \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators by their corresponding rectangle/lattice-path data and seek either:
   \[
   \ell_\gamma:M\otimes\mathbb Q\to\mathbb Q,\qquad
   \ell_\gamma(\Lambda_+M)=0,
   \]
   with evaluation matrix \((\ell_\gamma(s_\mu))\) triangular with nonzero diagonal; or an equivalent symbolic triangular-rank proof for the classes of the \(N\) generators in \(M/\Lambda_+M\). Such a proof would yield rational dimension \(N\). Together with the spanning induced by the \(N\) homogeneous generators, claim-7 gives \(M/\Lambda_+M\cong\mathbb Z^N\).

7. Submit the source packet, parameter enumeration, matrices, rank outputs, and universal argument to an independent reviewer. Required review checks: source hypotheses, grading, parameter filters, LR projection, construction of \(M_d,D_d\), rank interpretation, and the universal triangularity argument.
